public import FormalConjecturesUtil


/-!
# Erdős Problem 946

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/946](https://www.erdosproblems.com/946)
 - [ErMi52] Erdős, P. and Mirsky, L., The distribution of values of the divisor function {$d(n)$}.
   Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) (1952), 257--271.
 - [Sp81] Spiro, C. A., The frequency with which an integral-valued, prime-independent,
   multiplicative or additive function of n divides a polynomial function of n.
 - [He84] Heath-Brown, D. R., The divisor function at consecutive integers.
   Mathematika 31 (1984), no. 2, 141--149.
 - [Hi85] Hildebrand, A., The divisor function at consecutive integers. Pacific J. Math.
   (1987), 307--319
 - [EPS87] Erdős, P., Pomerance, C., and Sarkőzy, A., On locally repeated values of
   arithmetic functions. III. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1987), 1--7.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Real
open scoped ArithmeticFunction.sigma

namespace Erdos946

/--
There are infinitely many $n$ such that $τ(n) = τ(n+1)$. Proved in [He84].
Here τ is the divisor counting function, which is `σ 0` in mathlib.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos946.lean#L75"]
theorem erdos_946 : {n : ℕ | σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 1)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
There are infinitely many $n$ such that $τ(n) = τ(n + 5040)$. Proved in [Sp81].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_946.variants.spiro_5040 : {n : ℕ | σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 5040)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/-- Number of $n \le x$ with $τ(n) = τ(n+1)$. -/
noncomputable def erdos946Count (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ((Finset.range (⌊x⌋₊ + 1)).filter (fun n => σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 1))).card

/--
The number of $n \le x$ with $τ(n) = τ(n+1)$ is at least $x / (\log x)^7$ for all sufficiently
large $x$. Proved in [He84].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_946.variants.heathbrown_lower_bound :
    (fun x => x / (x.log)^7) =O[atTop] erdos946Count := by
  sorry

/--
Improved lower bound in [Hi85]: $Ω(x / (\log \log x)^3)$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_946.variants.hildebrand_lower_bound :
    (fun x => x / (x.log.log)^3) =O[atTop] erdos946Count := by
  sorry

/--
Upper bound in [EPS87]: $O(x / \sqrt{\log \log x})$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_946.variants.upper_bound : erdos946Count =O[atTop] (fun x => x / √x.log.log ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos946

findings.description: The docstring says the count is 'at least x / (log x)^7', which specifies coefficient 1. The Lean statement correctly expresses only a lower bound up to a positive multiplicative constant: x/(log x)^7 = O(erdos946Count x). The theorem matches the source; the prose should mention the implied constant.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/946 states the bound as ≫ x/(log x)^7. Hildebrand, The divisor function at consecutive integers, p. 307, equation (1.1), also states Heath–Brown's result with ≫: https://msp.org/pjm/1987/129-2/pjm-v129-n2-p06-s.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to 'is at least a positive constant multiple of x / (log x)^7 for all sufficiently large x', or write the bound using ≫. Leave the Lean statement unchanged.

findings.description: The [He84] bibliography entry gives Mathematika 31 (1984), no. 2, pp. 141–149. The cited article appeared in issue 1, not issue 2. This does not affect the mathematical statements.
findings.source_evidence: The publisher-supplied Crossref record for DOI 10.1112/S0025579300010743 records volume 31, issue 1, pages 141–149, published June 1984: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1112/S0025579300010743.

reformulations.difference: The definition enumerates natural numbers starting at 0 using Finset.range (⌊x⌋₊ + 1), rather than explicitly counting positive integers n ≤ x.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: σ 0 0 = 0 whereas σ 0 1 = 1, so 0 is always filtered out. For n > 0, n ≤ ⌊x⌋₊ is equivalent to (n : ℝ) ≤ x, even when x is negative. Thus the filtered finset is exactly {n : ℕ | 0 < n ∧ (n : ℝ) ≤ x ∧ σ 0 n = σ 0 (n + 1)}. This exact set equality was proved in the scratch file.

review.notes: No substantive misformalization was found in any of the six declarations. In particular, Hildebrand's denominator really is (log log x)^3. Scratch files /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/bigo.lean compile without errors or warnings; they test small divisor counts and prove the counting-set and positive-constant Big-O equivalences, with only standard Lean axioms. All research-solved tags agree with the source. The linked external proof states exactly the main theorem, and its retrieved import tree contained no sorry/custom-axiom declarations; that external project was not independently rebuilt. Spiro's result was corroborated by Hildebrand's introduction and the source page; the thesis itself was not obtained.
